results.content: ## Moving from ‘what’ to ‘why’ to build robust, reliable, and truly intelligent systems. > tl;dr Current AI is great at finding correlations (“seeing”), but to become truly intelligent, it must understand cause and effect (“doing” and “imagining”). This post explains that causality is the key to building robust, generalizable, and trustworthy AI systems, moving beyond the limits of today’s correlation-based models. We’ve spent the last decade celebrating AI’s incredible ability to predict outcomes from data. However, I believe the next decade of AI will be defined not by its ability to predict, but by its ability to *understand* and *explain*. ### Causality among other key intelligence attributes such as Common Sense Reasoning, Embodied Cognition, Continual Learning, Long-Term Memory, Goal-Directed Behavior, and Theory of Mind, is the key to building robust, generalizable, and trustworthy AI systems, moving beyond the limits of today’s…. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.
